clue.text: Perfume from a bunch of flowers

explanation.surface: A scent coming from a gathered posy of blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the aroma of a wine or scent and a posy of cut blooms handed over as a gift.

clue.text: Excellent, excellent side!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Excellent, excellent side! (7)': BRAVO (excellent) gives five letters and 'side' defines the swagger, but no clue word gives the AD that must go inside; the clue looks cut short and no search found the full text.

clue.text: Pawnbroker in the family

explanation.definitionFit: Old slang calls a pawnbroker by this relative's title, and a parent's brother is a relation within one's kin.

clue.text: Investment in which one has confidence

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one
trust is faith or confidence in someone

explanation.surface: A safe place for money, one you feel sure about.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a description of a trusted investment; in Britain a UNIT TRUST is a pooled fund, like an American mutual fund.
explanation.definitionFit: A pooled fund in which savers buy shares is a form of investment.

clue.text: Teeny-weeny bikini for Georgia brown initially

indicators.note: brown is to come first, at the start, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A tiny swimsuit is chosen for a tanned woman named Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' says the colour word goes before the state abbreviation, though the clue prints them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A very skimpy bikini of Brazilian style with tiny side straps is known by this name.

clue.text: Hound a godly man in fit of resentment

indicators.note: the godly man and the a are placed inside the fit of resentment

parts.note: a miff is a petty fit of pique
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a godly man

explanation.surface: Someone pesters a holy man while he is in a sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' looks like a verb (pester) but is the noun, a breed of large dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, powerful guard dog breed is a kind of hound in the loose sense of dog.

clue.text: Resolved disputes and arranged school hols

explanation.definitionFit: To come to an agreement ends a quarrel, and setting the dates of school terms in effect fixes when the holidays fall.

clue.text: Booth needs to play for time

explanation.surface: A stallholder has to hang about waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A market stand is a small booth, and to delay or temporise is to put off acting.

clue.text: Inclined to get a Glenn miller classic

explanation.surface: Feeling like putting on a big-band record.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disposed or willing means feeling like it, and the phrase is also the title of a famous 1939 swing tune by that bandleader.

clue.text: As ever, editor made sudden attack

parts.note: for ay (also spelt aye) means forever, always

explanation.surface: An editor, typical of them, launched an abrupt assault on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: AY, also spelt AYE, is an old word for ever, so 'for ay' means for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a raid or sudden incursion, so to have raided is this past tense.

clue.text: Sold assets to fund special education

indicators.note: special suggests an unusual, reworked arrangement of the letters of education

explanation.surface: Belongings were sold off to pay for special-needs schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special education' reads as one phrase, but 'special' is the anagram signal working on EDUCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods put under the hammer to the highest bidder have been sold at a public sale.

clue.text: Central rafters replaced later

indicators.note: central means the inner letters of rafters, without its first and last

explanation.surface: The middle beams of a roof were renewed afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' is padding to the surface here: the inner letters of RAFTERS already give the answer in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens subsequently comes behind in time, which is an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Stop a retired cleric going to Thailand

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the cleric's word is read backwards

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, a cleric
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: Someone tries to prevent a retired vicar from moving to Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: To ward off or prevent something is to halt it before it happens.

clue.text: Army corps unfortunately blocked main road

indicators.note: blocked means the main road is obstructed by having something set inside it

parts.note: an artery is a major road or route
ill can mean badly or unluckily, as in ill-fated

explanation.surface: Military units sadly obstructed the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunners of an army, with their big guns, form a branch or corps of the force.

clue.text: Not even like the first three clues above

definitions.text: like the first three clues above

explanation.surface: Uneven, like the clues at the top of the list.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole value not divisible by two is uneven, and the opening across clues are numbered one, five and nine, all such values.

clue.text: Appearance of roué named in error

indicators.note: in error means the letters of roue named are set down wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A rake's look is described mistakenly.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bearing or outward manner is the way they look to others.

clue.text: Sadly Mabel beal is guilty

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters of Mabel beal are put into a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: Poor Mabel Beal is found to be in the wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at fault deserves censure, so is culpable or guilty.

clue.text: Family of children makes bachelor cross

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix, a cross

explanation.surface: Having lots of kids makes a single man grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective (angry) but means a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A brood is a set of young from one birth, used loosely of a household's offspring.

clue.text: Escape for brief trip abroad

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
away means away from home, abroad

explanation.surface: Getting away from it all on a short holiday overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A breaking free from captivity or a group is a flight or escape.

clue.text: Space traveller means to arrive on time

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the time letter follows

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: An astronaut intends to turn up punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on time' reads as punctual; split it, with 'on' putting T after the arrival word.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of ice and dust orbiting the sun travels through outer space.

clue.text: To live in sin is a firm custom

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a habit is a custom or practice

explanation.surface: Living together unmarried is now commonplace.
explanation.definitionFit: To share a home as a couple without marrying was once called living in sin.

clue.text: Mad master somehow acquired capital

indicators.note: somehow signals the letters of mad master are rearranged in some fashion

explanation.surface: A crazy teacher came into some money by some means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money in the surface; it is a capital city, of the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch capital city, famous for canals, is a national capital.

clue.text: It may catch the poacher off guard

definitions.text: It may catch the poacher off guard

parts.words: It may catch the poacher off guard
parts.note: reads as a gamekeeper's trick for surprising a poacher, and literally describes a hidden device that grips an unwary intruder's leg

explanation.definitionFit: A concealed spring trap set on estates to seize trespassers is the device meant.

clue.text: Man with skill believed to be sincere

parts.note: he stands for a man
art means skill or craft
felt can mean believed, as in felt it was right

explanation.surface: A skilled man is trusted as genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings that come from the heart are genuine or sincere.

clue.text: Article by army reservists shows character

parts.note: the is the definite article
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A piece by army volunteers reveals their nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter here, the eighth of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek letter is an alphabetic character.

clue.text: Thanks to many, it's understood

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
it's here supplies it

explanation.surface: Thanks to the crowd, the point is taken without saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is implied without being spoken, so silently understood.

clue.text: He adds 50 per cent sake to French wine

indicators.note: fifty per cent means half of the word sake, its second half

parts.note: vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A man mixes half rice wine with French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A common boy's first name stands for a man, a he.

clue.text: Fodder for doctor and companion

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Food for a doctor and his friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant is a legume grown as animal feed, hence fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This climbing pea-family plant is grown to feed livestock.

clue.text: Shattered on being left penniless

explanation.surface: Devastated at finding oneself with no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Something smashed has been broken into pieces, and a person with no money at all is skint.

clue.text: Wake in rural retreat

explanation.surface: A boat's trail in a quiet country hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: The water thrown back behind a moving boat forms its trail, and a sleepy out-of-the-way village is a quiet place.

clue.text: Seamen want oriental sauce

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, so seamen gives two of them
the second sailor, a tar, from the plural seamen
E is short for east, oriental

explanation.surface: Sailors crave a spicy Asian dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayonnaise dressing with capers and gherkins is a classic sauce for fish.

clue.text: Retail outlet offers trifles prior to dance

indicators.note: prior to means the trifles come before the dance

parts.note: toys can mean trifles, things of little value
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A shop sells knick-knacks before the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling playthings is a retail outlet.
